In mathematics, the '''Wu manifold''' is a [[5-manifold]] defined as a quotient space of [[Lie group|Lie groups]] appearing in the mathematical area of [[Lie theory]]. Due to its special properties it is of interest in [[algebraic topology]], [[cobordism theory]] and  [[spin geometry]]. The manifold was first studied and named after [[Wu Wenjun]].

== Definition ==
The [[special orthogonal group]] <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> embeds canonically in the [[special unitary group]] <math>\operatorname{SU}(n)</math>. The [[orbit space]]:

: <math>W:=\operatorname{SU}(3)/\operatorname{SO}(3)</math>

is the Wu manifold.<ref name=":13">{{cite web |access-date=2024-06-10 |author=Diamuid Crowley |date=2011 |language=en |pages=49–55 |title=5-manifolds: 1-connected |url=http://www.boma.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/data/33print.pdf |website=Bulletin of the Manifold Atlas}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name=":0" />

== Properties ==

* <math>W</math> is a [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] [[rational homology sphere]] (with non-trivial [[homology groups]] <math>H_0(W)\cong\mathbb{Z}</math>, <math>H_2(W)\cong\mathbb{Z}_2</math><ref>Barden 1965, Lemma 1.1. (ii)</ref> and <math>H_5(W)\cong\mathbb{Z}</math>), which is not a [[sphere]]. Since in four or lower dimensions, every simply connected rational homology sphere is in fact a sphere, <math>W</math> provides a counterexample of lowest possible dimension.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ruberman |first=Daniel |title=Simply Connected Embedded Spheres of Codimension One |url=https://library.slmath.org/books/Book32/files/ruberman.pdf |journal=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute Publications |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |publication-place=Cambridge |volume=32 |pages=229-232, bottom of p. 230 and Example 7 on p. 232}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Simply-connected rational homology spheres |url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/214727/simply-connected-rational-homology-spheres |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=[[MathOverflow]] |language=en}}</ref>
* <math>W</math> has the [[cohomology groups]]:<ref name=":13" />
*: <math>H^0(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=\mathbb{Z}_2</math>
*: <math>H^1(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=1</math>
*: <math>H^2(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=\mathbb{Z}_2</math>
*: <math>H^3(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=\mathbb{Z}_2</math>
*: <math>H^4(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=1</math>
*: <math>H^5(W;\mathbb{Z}_2)
=\mathbb{Z}_2</math>
* <math>W</math> is a generator of the [[oriented cobordism]] group <math>\Omega_5^{\operatorname{SO}}\cong\mathbb{Z}_2</math>.<ref name=":13" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Debray |first=Arun |title=Characteristic classes |url=https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/a.debray/lecture_notes/u17_characteristic_classes.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107194324/https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/a.debray/lecture_notes/u17_characteristic_classes.pdf |archive-date=2021-01-07 |access-date=2024-06-09}}</ref> This can be detected using the [[de Rham invariant]], a particular [[Stiefel–Whitney class|Stiefel–Whitney number]], which describes an [[isomorphism]] <math>w_2w_3\colon\Omega_5^\mathrm{SO}\rightarrow\mathbb{Z}_2</math>. Since the first Stiefel-Whitney class vanishes due to orientability, all other Stiefel-Whitney numbers automatically vanish. As a consequence, any orientable 5-manifold with non-vanishing de Rham invariant is orientable bordant to <math>W</math>, which for example includes the [[Dold manifold]] <math>P(2,1)=(S^1\times\mathbb{C}P^2)/\mathbb{Z}_2</math>. Both yield to each other under [[Surgery theory|surgery]] for [[Embedding|embeddings]] <math>S^2\times D^3\hookrightarrow W</math> and <math>S^1\times D^4\hookrightarrow P(2,1)</math> with common [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] <math>S^2\times S^3</math>. An oriented bordism is then given by the [[cartesian product]] of one manifold with the [[unit interval]] and then the corresponding surgery on one end.
* <math>W</math> has a non-vanishing second and third [[Stiefel–Whitney class]] as well as a non-vanishing third integral Stiefel–Whitney class:<ref>Barden 1965, Lemma 1.1.(v) and Lemma 1.2.</ref>
*: <math>w_2(W)\neq 0;</math>
*: <math>w_3(W)\neq 0;</math>
*: <math>W_3(W)\neq 0.</math>
* <math>W</math> can be [[Immersion (mathematics)|immersed]] in <math>\mathbb{R}^8</math>, but not in <math>\mathbb{R}^7</math>. This is because all simply connected 5-manifolds can be immersed in <math>\mathbb{R}^8</math> with the third integral Stiefel-Whitney class vanishing [[if and only if]] it can be reduced to <math>\mathbb{R}^7</math> and the second Stiefel-Whitney class vanishing if and only if it can be further reduced to <math>\mathbb{R}^6</math>. Both isn't the case due to the previous property.<ref>Barden 1965, Lemma 2.4.</ref>
* <math>W</math> is a [[Spinh manifold|spin<sup>h</sup> manifold]] which doesn't allow a [[Spinc structure|spin<sup>c</sup> structure]]. The latter property comes from the fact that a spin<sup>c</sup> structure implies a vanishing third Stiefel-Whitney class, which isn't the case here.
